Hi Priyom —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're ready to move forward with an annual committed prepay (approx $240k) for Redwood services for 2027. Before we sign, finance has a couple of asks so we can wire and set up the PO: 

- Can you confirm a recommended disbursement schedule (we'd prefer multiple monthly tranches rather than one lump sum)?
- What are your requirements for VAT evidence? We have operations in DE and FR and need clarity on whether we should share VAT certificates or if you will reverse-charge.
- Do you support escrow release triggers or a simple monthly invoice/credit drawdown?
- Preferred remittance: ACH (US) or SEPA transfer — we can do either but need bank details and the ledger schedule to populate our AP system.

Attaching the SOW for reference (Acumen_SOW_Q2_2027.pdf). Can you loop in billing/finance or provide a sample schedule we can share with our AP team?

Best,

From: priyom.das@redwoodinference.com <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2027-05-18T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Annual prepay mechanics and VAT evidence

Hi Elise —

Thanks — excited to get this operational. Proposed approach below based on what typically balances cashflow and control for both sides. High level: 25% activation upfront, then monthly drawdowns over 9 months, final reconciliation in month 13. Details: 

- Total committed: $240,000
- Upfront (activation): 25% = $60,000 (invoice on activation)
- Monthly tranche: 9 equal drawdowns of $18,000 starting the following calendar month after activation
- Reserve/reconciliation: final invoice month for usage true-up and leftover credit (~1 month after final drawdown)

Escrow vs. ledger: we can do a ledger-based drawdown tied to PO + monthly invoice (simpler) or an escrow for larger strategic deals. For $240k, recommended ledger drawdown with a PO and monthly invoice schedule. If you prefer escrow, we can route to legal and finance.

VAT handling (EU): 
- If Acumen provides valid EU VAT IDs for Germany and France, Redwood will issue invoices zero-rated under reverse-charge and state the buyer VAT ID on the invoice. 
- If no VAT ID provided, Redwood will issue invoices with applicable VAT per country.
- Required evidence: PDF of VAT registration for each EU entity (VAT certificate) and the PO.

AP inputs we need from you to set up the ledger schedule: PO number, preferred remittance currency and bank routing (ACH / SEPA / Wire), billing contact. I attached a simple invoice template and the schedule CSV we will publish once finance confirms.

Action items for Acumen: 
1) Share PO number and AP contact (payables@acumenai.com fine).
2) Attach VAT certs for DE/FR if available.
3) Confirm acceptance of proposed tranche dates (we'll draft the monthly invoice schedule once you confirm).

I'll loop in our finance lead (karthik_iyer) and LA (Lauren) for PO/ledger setup.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Head of Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwoodinference.com

Thanks — I will stand up the ledger entries and the monthly invoice schedule. A couple of operational notes: 

- Bank routing: Redwood accepts SEPA (EUR) and SWIFT wires (USD/EUR). For SEPA we will provide IBAN/BIC. For US ACH, we can provide routing + acct on request.
- Invoicing: We'll create one central invoice series referencing ACU-2027-1245. If Acumen provides DE/FR VAT IDs, we will apply reverse-charge on the central invoice and include the VAT IDs in the invoice body. If you prefer country-specific invoices, let us know.
- VAT evidence required: official VAT registration PDFs for both entities (German and French). Once we receive those, we mark the deal as reverse-charge eligible.

I have created the initial ledger schedule and attached it for your AP team to ingest. It includes invoice dates, amounts, invoice references, and expected remittance currency.

Next steps for Redwood finance (internal): 
1) Upload Ledger_Schedule_ACU-2027-1245.csv into billing system.
2) Set up monthly invoice automation with reminder on day 5 of each invoice month.
3) Hold funds in ledger credit; allow drawdown per monthly invoice until reconciliation.

I'll confirm bank details (IBAN/BIC) in a separate secured email to Acumen's payables to avoid exposing them on the thread.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
